items.name: Perplexity
items.why: Today’s Portable Computer launch with Nvidia is a clear local/edge inference trigger, and Reo shows High intent (53 events, 12 developers) despite Partner status—exceptional signal for a MAX conversation on efficient on-device serving.
items.message: Aravind — saw today’s coverage of Portable Computer and the Nvidia partnership for a local-first agent with zero token costs. That shift puts a premium on inference efficiency and hardware utilization versus cloud token defaults. Modular’s MAX engine is built for exactly that: high-throughput, low-latency serving that teams can deploy beside GPU stacks without locking into a single cloud path. If you’re evaluating runtimes for Portable Computer or related agent workloads, happy to share a short benchmark on local/edge serving cost and latency. Open to a 20-minute working session this week with whoever owns inference?

items.name: Liner
items.why: Today’s $36.1M Series C to take evidence-first AI search into enterprise is a clean new-logo funding trigger; Not in Salesforce and Moderate Reo support outreach now.
items.message: Luke — congrats on the $36.1M Series C and the push to bring evidence-first AI search to enterprise. Enterprise search and agent workloads are inference-sensitive on both latency SLAs and cost as concurrent users grow. Modular’s MAX engine helps teams hit those targets while staying flexible across model mixes (frontier and open). Since you are not yet in our Salesforce pipeline, I wanted to reach out while the raise is fresh. Open to a short intro this week on how MAX could support your enterprise scale-up?

items.name: Upstage
items.why: Solar Pro 4’s frontier-score launch plus EY Han Young and HP Korea sovereign/vertical partnerships, with Moderate Reo (10 events), is a strong Not-in-SF product trigger.
items.message: Sung — Solar Pro 4’s Artificial Analysis Index result and the EY Han Young / HP Korea partnerships suggest sovereign and vertical deployments are moving from eval into production. Those environments need controlled, high-performance serving with predictable unit economics. Modular’s MAX inference engine is a strong fit for on-prem and region-bound LLM serving alongside specialized hardware you already explore. We have seen recent engagement from Upstage developers and would like to connect while Solar Pro 4 is ramping. Can we set up a technical session this week on serving cost and latency for Solar?

items.name: Wispr Flow
items.why: The ~$2B valuation and fresh capital attention for real-time voice-to-text, plus Moderate Reo, make this a high-priority new-logo scale-up for latency-sensitive inference.
items.message: Tanay — Reuters’ report on Wispr Flow’s $2B valuation and the follow-on funding attention imply a steep ramp in always-on speech inference. Viral free-tier usage plus enterprise expansion usually stresses latency and serving cost at the same time. Modular’s MAX engine is built for high-throughput, low-latency model serving—relevant if you are optimizing beyond a single hosted path. Not seeing Wispr in Salesforce yet, so I wanted to reach out while the valuation news is current. Would a 20-minute call this week with your ML infra owner make sense?

items.name: Abridge

items.message: Shiv — saw the Business Wire / Fierce coverage that Abridge is opening context-aware clinical intelligence to every clinician at partner health systems. Broadening from documentation into always-on decision support typically multiplies real-time inference load and tightens latency SLAs. Modular’s MAX stack helps clinical AI teams keep quality high while improving throughput and unit economics at health-system scale. We have recent developer engagement from your domain and would like to align while the rollout is live. Open to a brief technical intro this week with the team owning model serving?

items.name: Gamma
items.why: Today’s acquisition of Accel-backed Lica to build an AI design research lab is a fresh new-logo M&A trigger that should expand generative design inference demand.
items.message: Grant — TechCrunch’s report that Gamma acquired Lica to build an AI design research lab suggests a near-term jump in generative design and multimodal inference. Integrating an acquired research stack often forces a rethink of serving cost, latency, and hardware utilization across product surfaces. Modular’s MAX engine is built to make those workloads faster and cheaper without locking you to a single host. Since Gamma is not in Salesforce yet, I wanted to reach out while the acquisition news is current. Open to a 20-minute conversation this week on inference needs post-Lica?
